literal: If [you would] prevent, prevent the separation of the beloved; otherwise, if he departs, reunion indeed [is] difficult.
translation: If you would prevent anything, prevent the departure of my beloved; for if he leaves, a reunion will indeed be impossible.
modern: தடுக்க நினைத்தால், அன்பானவரின் பிரிவைத் தடுத்து நிறுத்துங்கள்; இல்லையென்றால், அவர் பிரிந்து சென்றால் மீண்டும் இணைவது அரிது.
explanation: In this verse, the heroine expresses the depth of her distress over her lover's impending departure. She urges her companion that if there is anything to be prevented, it must be his separation ('pirivu'). The word 'amaintār' refers to the lover who is perfectly suited and deeply intimate with her. She warns that if he departs ('nīṅkiṉ'), a future reunion ('puṇarvu') will be impossible ('aritu'), implying that she will not survive the grief of his absence.
